one_liner: Intel's C crypto-primitives library (ex-IPP Crypto) with SHA-NI/AVX2/AVX-512 SHA-1/2/3 kernels; claimed but unbenchmarked alternative to OpenSSL.
what_it_does: A broad C library of cryptographic building blocks, formerly Intel IPP Cryptography: hashes (SHA-1/2, SHA3, SHAKE, MD5, SM3), AES/SM4 modes, RSA/ECC, ML-KEM/ML-DSA/LMS/XMSS and bignum. Hashing goes through its own API, not EVP. You pick a method object (ippsHashMethod_SHA256_TT(), ippsHashMethod_SHA3_256(), ...), then either call ippsHashMessage_rmf() for one shot or ippsHashInit_rmf/Update_rmf/Final_rmf on a state buffer you allocate after querying ippsHashGetSize_rmf. Length arguments are int, and every call returns an IppStatus code.
how_it_is_fast: The library contains several builds of each function: generic, SSE4.2 (y8), AVX2 (l9), AVX-512 Skylake (k0), AVX-512 Ice Lake (k1) and AVX10.2 (d1). A dispatcher picks one per CPU at init, and a second layer of feature checks turns on SHA-NI, the SHA512 and SM3 instructions (Lunar Lake/Arrow Lake), VAES and similar extensions. SHA-2 comes as hand-written NASM kernels: an AVX2 message schedule (pcpsha256l9as.asm), a SHA-NI path (pcpsha256nias.asm) and a SHA512-instruction path (pcpsha512l9ni.asm). SHA-3/SHAKE on AVX-512 builds use an assembly Keccak that keeps all 25 lanes in xmm0-xmm24 and uses vpternlogq/vprolq, with a 4-way variant used internally for SHAKE.
when_to_use: x86-64 C/C++ code that already uses IPP-style APIs or needs SHA-2, SHA-3/SHAKE, SM3, AES, RSA/ECC and ML-KEM/ML-DSA from one Apache-2.0 vendor library
Deployments on recent Intel parts where the SHA-NI, SHA512 or SM3 instruction paths and the AVX-512 Keccak kernel apply
Projects that need CAVP-tested algorithm implementations (certificates listed for the AVX-512 builds) and FIPS self-test hooks, and will do their own CMVP module validation
Kernel-mode or footprint-sensitive builds: supports non-PIC static builds, per-ISA single-CPU libraries, and a custom-library tool that trims unused functions
when_not_to_use: When you need a measured win over OpenSSL: no published first- or third-party SHA-2/SHA-3 numbers exist, and OpenSSL also dispatches at runtime to SHA-NI/AVX2 assembly

Hashing many independent streams in parallel: there is no public multi-buffer SHA-2/SHA-3 API (the multi-buffer library covers SM3 mb16 plus public-key and SM4 operations); see ISA-L Crypto for multi-buffer SHA
Non-x86 targets (ARM, RISC-V) or macOS: code paths are x86 only, and the 1.4.0 changelog says it removed outdated macOS-specific code; validated on RHEL 8 and Windows Server 2022
If you need a drop-in or a FIPS 140-3 certificate: the API is not EVP-compatible, and README_FIPS says the library is 'FIPS-Compliant' (CAVP only), not CMVP-certified
Lightweight builds: needs CMake, NASM and Python, plus OpenSSL 3.5.7+/BoringSSL/Tongsuo unless the multi-buffer part is disabled

integration.form: static lib and shared lib (CMake; can also be pulled in via add_subdirectory)
integration.dependencies: Build: CMake 3.18+, NASM (3.01 tested), Python 3.12; OpenSSL 3.5.7+/BoringSSL/Tongsuo only for the crypto_mb multi-buffer part (drop with -DNO_CRYPTO_MB=TRUE)
integration.min_toolchain: C; tested with GCC 8.5-16.1, Clang 16/21, MSVC 19.44 (VS 2022), Intel oneAPI icx 2026.2
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux/Windows (32-bit IA-32 deprecated); ISA paths y8 SSE4.2, l9 AVX2, k0/k1 AVX-512, d1 AVX10.2, plus a generic mx build; crypto_mb k1 also validated on FreeBSD
integration.thread_safety: README claims a thread-safe design, with caller-allocated per-operation state and no hidden allocation; issue #106 (ML-KEM concurrent stack smash, fixed) shows this has had bugs

gotchas: Fetch the hash-method pointer once, outside hot loops: calling ippsHashMethod_SHA256_TT() per hash writes a shared static and collapsed multi-thread scaling on a 24-core Xeon (issue #93)

In the develop source, the first call to ippsHashMethod_SHA256_TT() ends with the non-SHA-NI update routine; only later calls switch it to SHA-NI, and all states share that static. So a pointer fetched once may not use SHA-NI; benchmark it
Update/Message lengths are int, so feed inputs over 2 GiB in chunks; the non-_rmf hash APIs are slated for removal in 3.0.0 (issue #107)
develop is an unstable snapshot; production code lives on cryptography-primitives_<release> branches. Pin a release, and use -DIPPCP_FIPS_MODE=on for the FIPS self-test build
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose it over ISA-L Crypto or sha2-with-c-intrinsic when you want one maintained Intel library that covers single-stream SHA-2 (SHA-NI and SHA512-instruction paths), SHA-3/SHAKE and SM3 alongside ciphers and PQC, with CAVP certificates. Use ISA-L Crypto for multi-buffer throughput across many streams, and BLAKE3/KangarooTwelve if you can change the hash function.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing has been measured publicly. The README, OVERVIEW, BUILD and CHANGELOG say only 'fast' and 'optimized performance for SHA3-...', with no hardware, compiler or baseline named. The repo ships a perfsys tool (ps_ippcp) to benchmark its own functions but publishes no results and no OpenSSL comparison, so any speedup over OpenSSL SHA-2/SHA-3 is unverified.
status_note: Actively maintained by Intel (last commit 2026-09-25, v2.4.0 changelog, 3.0.0 API cleanup under discussion) under Apache-2.0, so usable in proprietary code. It is a large build, not something to vendor as a snippet.
